operation_type.description: Provide the operation type. Allowed values: Create, Modify. Synonyms must be normalized to the canonical value.
operation_type.x-a2at-value-constraint: Allowed canonical values: Create, Modify. Normalize synonyms to the canonical value instead of treating them as out-of-range: Add / Implement / Establish / Deploy / Set Up / Provision / New / Enable / Activate / Configure are all Create; Update / Adjust / Change / Revise / Edit are all Modify.

task_description.description: Dynamically provide the task description based on the operation type (Create/Modify).
examples: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output).
task_description.x-a2at-value-constraint: When the type is [Create]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output). When the type is [Modify]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), output a wireless network energy saving plan that achieves the wireless network energy saving goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target). The value must always be non-null. Output the fixed text verbatim; there is no need to replace [Task Object](#task-object), [Task Context](#task-context), [Task Target](#task-target) or [Expected Output](#expected-output) with actual slot values — these are in-document anchor links, not placeholders. When the task_target slot has no value, the description must not claim that a goal is defined and must not reference a missing goal.

task_object.description: Explicitly specify the energy saving coverage scope information, a geographic or logical area (e.g., district-level administrative unit). The area information is a required parameter.
task_object.x-a2at-value-constraint: Area name. A named region (a specific region name such as "ExampleRegion" or "Slice A") is valid. Only anonymous vague descriptions that carry no concrete region name, such as "test area", "sites in this area", "all communities", "indoor communities", or "outdoor communities", must report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Area' and actual describing what is missing. Only one region name is allowed; if the input specifies multiple regions, report slot.constraint_violated.

task_target.description: Define the quantitative or qualitative goals the task must achieve. Quantitative and qualitative goals cannot be selected at the same time, and the default is a qualitative goal.
task_target.x-a2at-value-constraint: Only an explicit energy saving gain target belongs in this slot. When the input states a percentage gain target (for example 'Set the gain target to 30%' or 'energy saving gain target: 30%'), write it as 'energy saving gain target: X%'. A range (for example '20%-30%') reports slot.constraint_violated; the single gain value must be stated explicitly. Every other goal must NOT be placed in this slot and must stay verbatim in task_context: a qualitative mode (Aggressive, Conservative, Lossless Experience, Lossy Experience, 'maximize energy saving', 'user experience first', 'energy saving first', 'maximize KPI assurance', 'high GS'), a numeric throughput/rate/UX target, a 'Power Savings Ratio' or 'power saving ratio' value, and a carrier-shutdown or frequency instruction. When the input states no explicit percentage gain target, the value is null; never write 'Not provided', a section name, or a mode as the value.

task_context.description: Provide the background and context information for task execution.
examples: Cell RAT for energy saving: NR; Energy saving time range: start time "08:00:00", end time "12:00:00"; Time-segmented rate guarantee goal: {00:00~06:00,2Mbps}, {06:00~18:00,10Mbps}.
task_context.x-a2at-value-constraint: 1. Cell RAT: LTE, NR, LNR, all (synonyms are listed in the [terminology] section below). When the input does not state a RAT, do not add a Cell RAT line at all (the separate structured-intent extraction defaults to ALL); a frequency numbering scheme such as NR-ARFCN or EARFCN does not by itself specify a RAT. Invalid values (e.g. '3G') report slot.constraint_violated. 2. Cross-task reference: if the input inherits parameters by referencing an earlier task (e.g. 'same as the previous task') but multiple earlier tasks exist and the reference is ambiguous, report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Task reference'. Do not silently pick one candidate; set value to null. Example: input mentions two earlier tasks (one covering ExampleRegionA with NR, 00:00:00~06:00:00, 5 Mbps floor; the other covering ExampleRegionB with NR, 00:00:00~06:00:00, 2 Mbps floor) and then says 'same as the previous task' -- the reference is ambiguous, report slot.constraint_violated; do not choose the second task's 2 Mbps floor. 3. Energy saving time range, recurring daily; if omitted, full-period energy saving. Write it as its own line in the form 'Energy saving time range: start time "HH:MM:SS", end time "HH:MM:SS"'. Rate goal is guaranteed only within this range. 4. Carrier frequencies that can be turned off. Preserve the operator's own sentence and frequency notation (e.g. 'EARFCN 1600 can be shut down during the energy-saving period.'); do not rewrite it as a label/value list. When carrier turn-off is requested but concrete frequency points are missing, report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Carrier frequencies'. A frequency must be a specific number (e.g. 1600), not an approximation (e.g. 'approximately 1600'); approximations report slot.constraint_violated. 5. Preserve the operator's own wording for rate, UX and qualitative goals; do not normalize them. A bare rate or UX statement (e.g. 'guarantee 10 Mbps from 19:00 to 22:00', 'Ensure the UX target is at least 10 Mbps', 'Set the SLA to 10', 'ensuring user experience for 720p video') stays verbatim in this slot. Do NOT convert it to a time-segmented {HH:MM~HH:MM,NMbps} segment and do NOT derive a Mbps value from a bitrate or terminology term such as 720p, 1080p or 4K. Only when the operator explicitly gives per-window rates (e.g. '10 Mbit/s from 08:00 to 12:00 and 5 Mbit/s from 11:00 to 18:00') render them as time-segmented segments in the form {HH:MM-HH:MM: NMbps}; keep any surrounding operator sentence. Qualitative modes ('maximize energy saving', 'user experience first', 'energy saving first', 'high GS', 'maximize KPI assurance') stay verbatim; do not map them to Aggressive/Conservative/Lossless/Lossy and do not move them to task_target. A mode value that is not one of these recognized modes or their listed synonyms (for example 'green' or 'eco') reports slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Energy saving mode'. Time windows MUST NOT overlap and must fall within the energy-saving execution period; overlapping windows report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. Time windows are half-open intervals of one day: 00:00 is the start of the day and 24:00 is the end of that same day. A window ending at 24:00 (e.g. 05:00~24:00) therefore does NOT continue into 00:00 of that day or the next day, and does NOT overlap a window that starts at 00:00. Windows that merely touch at one endpoint (e.g. 00:00~03:00 and 03:00~05:00, or 00:00~03:00 and 05:00~24:00) do not overlap; only windows that share more than an endpoint (e.g. 05:00~08:00 and 07:00~10:00) overlap. Vague time descriptions (busy/idle/peak/off-peak) report slot.constraint_violated. A vague rate (e.g. 'maximize the rate' without a number) reports slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Guaranteed rate'. When a rate change is tied to a concrete time range but no rate value is given, keep the operator's sentence and allow the missing rate: for a site-level or outage Modify the server negotiates the value, so do not report slot.not_provided merely because the input says 'modify the guaranteed throughput target' without a number. 6. In outage/modify scenarios, preserve the operator's sentence, including the affected site list (concrete site names, not 'sites in this area' or '10 sites'), the outage start/end time and the background event wording. Missing concrete outage time reports slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Outage start/end time'. A concrete site list is required: a count such as '10 sites' or 'several sites', or 'sites in this area', is not a site list, so report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list' (this applies to Modify too). Outage duration must be a single specific number (e.g. 3 hours), not a range (e.g. '2 or 3 hours'); ranges report slot.constraint_violated. Do not rewrite a bare rate into segments; item 5 governs rate formatting.

expected_output.description: When the task object is a geographic/logical area, output the intent report for the network energy saving task.
expected_output.x-a2at-value-constraint: Basic information about the intent execution result: area, intent goal achievement status. Detailed information about the intent execution result: energy saving gain achievement status (current energy saving gain goal, actual energy saving gain percentage, target adjustment suggestions), rate goal achievement status (current rate goal, actual rate, target adjustment suggestions).
